By contrast, center-ground outlets like NPR, Politico, and the Financial Times used plain factual verbs — "rejects," "blocks," "rejects" — with no adversarial framing. The Federalist, at the right end, described the ruling neutrally as "SCOTUS Blocks Trump's Mail-In Voting Order," treating it as a policy setback without dramatization, representing a noticeably more restrained register than the left-leaning outlets.
